root_cause.text: The Bluetooth HCI event path called `hci_store_wake_reason()` from `hci_event_packet()` before `hci_event_func()` had performed per-event minimum-length validation, letting a short `skb` reach `bacpy()`/wake-address parsing in `net/bluetooth/hci_event.c` without bounds checking.
root_cause.evidence: The commit message says `hci_store_wake_reason() is called from hci_event_packet() immediately after stripping the HCI event header but before hci_event_func() enforces the per-event minimum payload length from hci_ev_table`, and the patch removes that early call and instead invokes `hci_store_wake_reason()` only inside validated handlers such as `hci_conn_request_evt()`, `hci_conn_complete_evt()`, `le_conn_complete_evt()`, and LE advertising report handlers.

agent_logs.root_cause_candidate: The Bluetooth HCI event path called `hci_store_wake_reason()` from `hci_event_packet()` before `hci_event_func()` had performed per-event minimum-length validation, letting a short `skb` reach `bacpy()`/wake-address parsing in `net/bluetooth/hci_event.c` without bounds checking.
agent_logs.evidence_points: The commit message says `hci_store_wake_reason() is called from hci_event_packet() immediately after stripping the HCI event header but before hci_event_func() enforces the per-event minimum payload length from hci_ev_table`, and the patch removes that early call and instead invokes `hci_store_wake_reason()` only inside validated handlers such as `hci_conn_request_evt()`, `hci_conn_complete_evt()`, `le_conn_complete_evt()`, and LE advertising report handlers.

intent_record.intent_summary: Add a lock-annotation declaration for wake-reason handling to ensure callers hold `hdev->lock`.
intent_record.what: A forward declaration was added for a new static function `hci_store_wake_reason(struct hci_dev *hdev, const bdaddr_t *bdaddr, u8 addr_type)` and it is annotated with `__must_hold(&hdev->lock)`.
intent_record.how: This does not change runtime logic by itself; it introduces a declaration that enforces, at compile-time/static analysis time, that any caller must hold `hdev->lock` when using the function, helping prevent incorrect locking usage around wake-reason storage.

intent_record.intent_summary: Record the wake reason for completed BR/EDR connections during connection event handling.
intent_record.what: A call to hci_store_wake_reason(hdev, &ev->bdaddr, BDADDR_BREDR); was inserted immediately after hci_dev_lock(hdev); in hci_conn_complete_evt(). No other code in the hunk was changed.
intent_record.how: When a Bluetooth Classic (BR/EDR) connection completion event is handled, the code now records the wake reason for the peer address before continuing with existing connection checks and processing. This enables the kernel to track that the device may have been woken by this BR/EDR connection event.

intent_record.intent_summary: Store the wake reason for incoming BR/EDR connection requests under lock before processing the event.
intent_record.what: Three statements were inserted at the start of hci_conn_request_evt(): it now acquires the HCI device lock, calls hci_store_wake_reason(hdev, &ev->bdaddr, BDADDR_BREDR), and then releases the lock before the existing comment and connection rejection logic.
intent_record.how: At runtime, an incoming BR/EDR connection request now records the wake reason associated with the peer Bluetooth address under the device lock, which updates internal state used for wake tracking/diagnostics before the rest of the event handling continues.

intent_record.intent_summary: Record the wake reason for synchronous BR/EDR connection completion events before processing the connection.
intent_record.what: A call to hci_store_wake_reason(hdev, &ev->bdaddr, BDADDR_BREDR) was inserted in hci_sync_conn_complete_evt() immediately after hci_dev_lock(hdev) and before the lookup of the connection object.
intent_record.how: When a synchronous BR/EDR connection completion event is processed, the code now records the wake reason associated with the peer Bluetooth address before continuing with connection handling. This allows the device to preserve or report why the system woke for this event.

intent_record.intent_summary: Record the wake reason on LE connection completion so the connection event is properly attributed.
intent_record.what: A call to hci_store_wake_reason(hdev, bdaddr, bdaddr_type); was inserted near the start of le_conn_complete_evt() immediately after acquiring hci_dev_lock(hdev).
intent_record.how: At runtime, when an LE connection completes, the code now records the wake reason associated with the peer Bluetooth address and address type before continuing with the rest of the connection-complete handling. This enables later tracking or attribution of why the controller/device woke up for the connection event.

intent_record.intent_summary: Record the remote device as a wake reason when handling LE PA sync transfer received events.
intent_record.what: A call to hci_store_wake_reason(hdev, &ev->bdaddr, ev->bdaddr_type); was inserted in hci_le_past_received_evt() immediately after hci_dev_lock(hdev) and before hci_dev_clear_flag(hdev, HCI_PA_SYNC).
intent_record.how: When a LE Periodic Advertising Sync Transfer received event is handled, the controller now records the peer address and address type as a wake reason while the device lock is held, allowing the Bluetooth stack to track what remote device may have caused the wakeup.

intent_record.intent_summary: Record the advertiser address as a wake reason when processing LE advertising reports.
intent_record.what: A call to hci_store_wake_reason(hdev, &info->bdaddr, info->bdaddr_type) was inserted in hci_le_adv_report_evt() immediately after the existing length check and before the advertisement length handling logic.
intent_record.how: When a LE advertising report is processed, the controller now records the advertising device address and address type as a wake reason before continuing with RSSI extraction and advertisement report processing. This allows the system to attribute a wake-up event to the nearby BLE advertiser that triggered it.

intent_record.intent_summary: Store the wake reason for LE extended advertising reports so wake events are correctly attributed to the reporting device.
intent_record.what: A call to hci_store_wake_reason(hdev, &info->bdaddr, info->bdaddr_type); was inserted in hci_le_ext_adv_report_evt() immediately after the existing length check and before evt_type is derived.
intent_record.how: At runtime, the handler now records the wake reason for each valid LE extended advertising report using the peer's Bluetooth address and address type, allowing the device to attribute wake events to the advertising source.

intent_record.intent_summary: Record the PA sync peer as the wake reason when a LE PA sync is established.
intent_record.what: A call to `hci_store_wake_reason(hdev, &ev->bdaddr, ev->bdaddr_type);` was inserted immediately after `hci_dev_lock(hdev);` in `hci_le_pa_sync_established_evt()` before `HCI_PA_SYNC` is cleared.
intent_record.how: When a LE PA sync establishment event is handled, the controller now records the Bluetooth address and address type as the wake reason while the device lock is held. This preserves the event source information for later wake attribution and ensures it is captured during sync establishment processing.

intent_record.intent_summary: Store the wake reason for LE direct advertising reports before handling them.
intent_record.what: Inside hci_le_direct_adv_report_evt(), a call to hci_store_wake_reason(hdev, &info->bdaddr, info->bdaddr_type) was inserted in the loop before process_adv_report() is invoked for each received direct advertising report.
intent_record.how: At runtime, each direct advertising report now records the advertiser address and address type as a wake reason before the report is processed, allowing the system to track which remote device may have caused the controller to wake the host.

intent_record.intent_summary: Refactor wake-reason recording to accept a pre-parsed address under an existing lock, simplifying the helper and preserving wake source tracking.
intent_record.what: The function `hci_store_wake_reason()` was changed from taking `(struct hci_dev *hdev, u8 event, struct sk_buff *skb)` and parsing multiple HCI event payload formats internally to taking `(struct hci_dev *hdev, const bdaddr_t *bdaddr, u8 addr_type)`, adding a `__must_hold(&hdev->lock)` annotation, replacing `hci_dev_lock()/unlock()` with `lockdep_assert_held(&hdev->lock)`, simplifying the control flow to early returns, and unconditionally storing the provided address/type when the device is suspended and no wake reason has been recorded.
intent_record.how: Runtime behavior is now simplified so this helper no longer inspects raw skb/event contents or acquires the device lock itself; instead, callers must already hold the lock and pass in the wake source address directly. If the device is not suspended or a wake reason is already set, it does nothing; if no address is available, it records `MGMT_WAKE_REASON_UNEXPECTED`; otherwise it records `MGMT_WAKE_REASON_REMOTE_WAKE` and saves the given BD_ADDR and address type.

intent_record.intent_summary: Move wake-reason handling to after event processing under lock to ensure correct and safe wake reason tracking.
intent_record.what: The call to hci_store_wake_reason(hdev, event, skb) was removed from before hci_event_func(), and replaced with a post-processing sequence that locks the HCI device, calls hci_store_wake_reason(hdev, NULL, 0), and then unlocks the device after hci_event_func() returns.
intent_record.how: Wake reason storage is no longer tied to the raw incoming event packet at the start of hci_event_packet(); instead, it is cleared or updated after event handling completes, under the device lock. This changes the timing and context of wake-reason tracking and likely avoids using the packet data after it may have been consumed or transformed by event handlers.

Move wake-reason handling to after event processing under lock to ensure correct and safe wake reason tracking.
Store the wake reason for incoming BR/EDR connection requests under lock before processing the event.
Record the wake reason on LE connection completion so the connection event is properly attributed.
Record the remote device as a wake reason when handling LE PA sync transfer received events.
Record the advertiser address as a wake reason when processing LE advertising reports.
Store the wake reason for LE extended advertising reports so wake events are correctly attributed to the reporting device.

consistency_review.core_intent: Record and defer wake-reason handling for BR/EDR connection completion events so it occurs safely during/after event processing under lock.

relevance_review.reason: The change only adds a lock-annotation requirement for wake-reason handling, which is a concurrency/documentation constraint. It does not address the root cause of the vulnerability: premature parsing of short HCI event buffers before minimum-length validation in the event path.

The changes move wake-reason handling out of the early HCI event packet path and defer it to safer per-event processing, which directly addresses the root cause where hci_store_wake_reason() could be reached before minimum-length validation and access short skbs unsafely.

The change targets the same HCI event path and adds wake-reason handling for incoming connection requests before event processing, which is directly related to the vulnerable early call into wake-reason parsing before minimum-length validation.

The change is about recording wake reasons for LE connection completion attribution, not about fixing the short-skb / minimum-length validation issue in the HCI event path that led to unsafe wake-address parsing.

The change is about recording a wake reason for a specific LE event, but the reported vulnerability is a bounds-checking issue in the generic HCI event path where hci_store_wake_reason() could be called before minimum-length validation. This group does not address that validation order or short-skb handling.

The group changes the Bluetooth HCI event handling path to record an advertiser address as a wake reason during LE advertising report processing, which is the same wake-reason parsing path implicated in the short-skb bounds-checking flaw.

This change is about attributing wake reasons for LE extended advertising reports, not about fixing the short-skb/bounds-checking issue in hci_event_packet()/hci_store_wake_reason() described in the root cause.
The change adds wake-reason handling for LE PA sync establishment and is unrelated to the HCI event short-skb bounds-checking issue in hci_event_packet()/hci_store_wake_reason().

The change is in the Bluetooth HCI event path and explicitly stores the wake reason for LE direct advertising reports before handling them, which matches the vulnerable early-call pattern described in the root cause.

The change directly refactors wake-reason recording in the Bluetooth HCI event path, which is the area implicated by the short-skb/bounds-checking issue. Even though it simplifies the helper, it is still tied to the vulnerable wake-address parsing logic in hci_event.c.

candidates.rationale: This call happens in the global event path before hci_event_func() performs per-event minimum-length validation, so a short skb can reach hci_store_wake_reason() and its bacpy()/address parsing without bounds checks.

vuln_statements.explanation: This call occurs in the global HCI event path before hci_event_func() performs per-event minimum-length validation, allowing a short skb to reach wake-reason parsing and bacpy()/address handling without bounds checking.

bic_trace_step.reason: The snippet clearly shows the vulnerable pattern: `hci_event_packet()` now calls `hci_store_wake_reason(hdev, event, skb);` immediately after `skb_pull(skb, HCI_EVENT_HDR_SIZE);` and before the per-event parsing/validation in the `switch (event)` body. The helper then dereferences event-specific fields directly from `skb->data`, e.g. `const struct hci_ev_conn_complete *conn_complete = (void *)skb->data;`, `const struct hci_ev_conn_request *conn_request = (void *)skb->data;`, and for LE meta events `u8 num_reports = *ptr;` followed by `bacpy(&hdev->wake_addr, ...)`. Because the root cause is that this wake-reason parsing runs before `hci_event_func()` has performed minimum-length validation, a short skb could reach these dereferences without bounds checking. There is no fix present here; the code does not add length checks before the direct field accesses, so `is_fixed` is false.
